Empirical reference study and repeatable process specification | Josh | 10 November 2026
The final edit of What to Say to Tough Executive Questions shows that the main task is choosing complete takes, then
placing safe joins. Silence trimming alone cannot reproduce it. The proposed process should preserve a source time
map, synchronize the good microphone, transcribe and align speech, remove abandoned takes, treat nonverbal events
separately, and review uncertain joins before rendering.

Reference and measurement method
Reference selection matters. The current project and export map to 15 retained clips and 408.733 s of timeline audio.
Older notes describing 14 clips or roughly 413 s are not the current reference. The analysis uses the direct A1 source
discontinuities in the final Premiere project, rather than inferring edit decisions from overall duration.
The source is the enhanced Wireless PRO WAV used in the final A1 edit, not a separately verified raw microphone
recording. Source PCM was read at 48 kHz. Its 10 ms RMS p10 is -87.61 dBFS and p95 is -21.00 dBFS; these describe
an enhanced signal, not the physical room noise floor. Calibrate again if the raw recording or enhancement chain
changes.
Premiere stores 254016000000 ticks per second and approximately 8467191533 ticks per nominal 30 fps video frame.
Preserve tick and sample coordinates; do not repeatedly round through displayed seconds. The sub-millisecond timing
approximations do not justify adding or deleting content.
- For every retained clip, three independent positions were correlated against the export, for 45 total windows.
 Correlation windows were up to 1.4 s and evaluated at 16 kHz effective sampling. The matching export lag was
21.302 to 21.373 ms. This validates correspondence throughout the sequence but is not an exhaustive
sample-by-sample or perceptual review.
- The 28.925 ms difference between timeline end and decoded export duration is recorded explicitly. It is not used to
 invent a missing edit or to rescale all source timestamps. Container, codec and final-sample behavior require separate
checking when implementing export verification.
- Acoustic offsets use nonoverlapping 10 ms RMS windows in the native microphone PCM. At each source cut, the
 method searches up to two seconds backward or forward for a window above a stated level. Outgoing offset is the
time from the last active window end to source out. Incoming offset is the time from source in to the next active window
start.
- Offsets therefore measure threshold-level acoustic activity, not speech onset, consonant completion or word alignment
 accuracy. A 10 ms measurement grid, enhancement artifacts, breaths and quiet consonants affect them. Zero means
activity reached the boundary at that threshold, not proof of an audible fault.
- Premiere words were associated with intervals by word midpoint. The mapped final transcript is the retained subset of
 source words, not an independently transcribed export. Independent source and export ASR should be retained
separately and reconciled, not silently substituted for ground truth.

Synchronization and evidence quality
Camera and microphone synchronization
The project places microphone source time 3.6999963 s ahead of camera source time. Six 10 s speech-envelope checks
using a 5 ms grid and 25 ms smoothing find 3.705 to 3.710 s, with correlations 0.830 to 0.886. This corroborates the
project offset within one nominal 30 fps frame. Different processing creates about 5 to 10 ms acoustic ambiguity; these
checks do not prove lip sync, establish drift or justify retiming.
This approximately 3.7 s camera/microphone relationship is separate from the approximately 21.3 ms microphone/export
decoded-audio lag. The two offsets must never be substituted for each other.

Three different questions must be kept separate. An amplitude detector can answer only the first one directly. The

Current cutter audit and replay
The current path is helper/dajoshi_cut.py plan_cut into cleancut.acoustic_keeps. Its acoustic stage is an energy-based
interval rule, not semantic take selection and not an event classifier.
- It computes 10 ms RMS, smooths power over 50 ms, estimates a p10 noise level and sets auto threshold to p10 + 5
 dB, clamped between -65 and -20 dBFS. On this enhanced source the effective automatic threshold is -65 dBFS. It
uses p95 as a reference speech level.
- Above-threshold runs separated by less than 150 ms are merged before filtering. All events shorter than 80 ms are
 dropped even when the optional sounds switch is off. With the switch on, events shorter than 1.2 s and quieter than
p95 minus 11 dB are also dropped. These features do not identify coughs.
- Later pause merging and padding can reinclude an event that was previously dropped. Event protection and deletion
 therefore need an explicit interval representation that survives later stages.
- Defaults are maximum pause 450 ms, lead 80 ms and tail 100 ms. The UI sets lead to 0.8 times tail. The older 150 ms
 min_cut parameter is not the active algorithm.
- The flubs path uses transcript-word deletion ranges and generic language-model instructions to keep the final
 complete take while preserving emphasis. It has not learned this editor style, and does not automatically run acoustic
cleanup afterward. Its boundary snap searches plus or minus 80 ms for low RMS with 20 ms word guards; its
threshold parameter is unused.

Repeatable pipeline specification
The output of this work is a design and testable process, not a deployed edit. The order below preserves enough
evidence to explain and reverse every proposed deletion.
1 Ingest and preserve coordinates
Register original camera and microphone files with hashes, channel count, sample rate, rational frame rate, frame count,
duration and time-base metadata. Preserve the originals. Define source camera time, microphone PCM sample time and
edited output time as distinct coordinates; do not use rounded displayed timecode as the interchange format.
2 Run the green screen pre step without retiming
Background replacement should preserve source timestamps, rational frame rate, frame count and audio. The pre-step
emits the processed video plus a sidecar describing its source and timing. If any frames are removed, repeated or
retimed, it must emit an explicit piecewise map back to source. Reject a silently retimed result. Image-only processing is
not permission to change recording duration.
3 Choose and synchronize the good microphone
Select the intended good mic explicitly or propose it for review. Match multiple separated speech anchors to camera
audio, estimate offset and test affine drift. Model camera time as a + b times microphone time. Validate residuals near
the beginning, middle and end; use a piecewise map or manual review if residuals exceed a stated tolerance. This
recording's 21.3 ms source-to-export lag is not the camera-to-microphone offset and must not be reused as one.
4 Transcribe and align the source
Transcribe the full good-mic source, with word times and uncertainty. Align text back to PCM and retain raw ASR
separately from corrected text. Keep short uncertain tokens and nonverbal spans as reviewable evidence. Use camera
audio only as a sync or fallback source, rather than replacing a verified mic with mixed export audio.
5 Propose repeated take removal
Group nearby restarts using lexical overlap, syntax, repeated meaning and acoustic pauses. Propose retaining the last
complete usable take, but check that earlier material adds no unique fact, qualification or intentional emphasis. The rule
is a candidate-generation default, not always keep the last take. Record exactly what is removed and why. Send partial
words, mixed complete takes and meaning changes to review.
6 Build a separate event and pause track
Before phrase merging, mark candidate breaths, coughs, throat clears, clicks, silence and uncertain speech on the
source time axis. Keep event classification confidence separate from speech alignment confidence. Remove a nonverbal
event only when its class and surrounding speech safety meet the approved pilot criteria. Otherwise retain and queue it.
7 Refine joins then export proposals
After semantic deletions, refine the outgoing and incoming sides independently using speech and event evidence.
Preserve natural intra-phrase pauses and emphasis. Produce conservative EDL and JSON with source mappings,
reason codes, confidence, uncertainty and review snippets. Apply only reviewed proposals to copies, then render and
validate the result.

10
Choosing a clean join
Speech detection and boundary search serve different purposes. A speech-detection threshold helps propose protected
speech intervals; a boundary-search level helps evaluate candidate edges only inside a region already judged safe. Do
not use one global amplitude number to perform both jobs.
Estimate local noise from validated non-speech windows rather than equating global p10 with the room floor. Use
separate onset and offset thresholds, or hysteresis, plus agreement between ASR, voice activity detection, spectral cues
and energy to protect speech. These are proposed engineering rules, not evaluated improvements in this study.
Boundary search
- Use alignment to identify the first and last intended phonemes, then extend into safe background. A low-energy valley
 inside a fricative or quiet syllable is not a safe boundary just because RMS is low.
- Set a bounded search around each proposed word boundary and return multiple scored candidates. Treat short cut
 leads such as cut 3, and the ambiguous incoming regions at cuts 5 and 13, as required review cases. A 20 ms
transcript guard does not establish phonetic safety.
- Separate join placement from pause policy. Between continuous intended phrases, retain the source pause unless a
 contextual rule proposes shortening it. A numerical ceiling alone cannot decide whether a pause is rhetorical, cognitive
or an interruption.
- Keep any confirmed event removal as an explicit excluded interval. Later padding and phrase merging must not
 reinclude it silently. If safe padding would cross an excluded event or word, flag the conflict rather than overriding one
stage invisibly.
- Quantize only at the output stage. Preserve sample-accurate audio ranges internally, derive video boundaries using
 the verified time map, and report any frame-rounding displacement. Audio and video edit lists must refer to the same
intended content.
Refine only within an approved safe non-speech band. Within that band, prefer a low-energy sample crossing and small
amplitude discontinuity, while preserving sufficient handles. If needed, test an optional 2 to 5 ms fade confined to
non-speech. That duration is a proposed engineering safeguard, not a measured editor preference. Never crossfade
syllables or erase breaths implicitly.
The largest measured raw source hard-splice sample jump across the 14 reference joins is -49.25 dBFS, at cut 13. This
makes seam discontinuities measurable, but does not establish that a click is or is not audible. A zero-jump case is
recorded as -200 dBFS in the diagnostic file; this is a numerical sentinel, not a physical noise reading. Listening and
rendered-output checks remain necessary.

Cough and throat clear handling
The current short-and-quiet heuristic is insufficient: coughs can be loud or adjacent to speech, while short quiet events
can be legitimate words, consonants or breaths. Merging before classification can absorb an event into speech; later
expansion can undo a removal. A separate event track and post-merge exclusion check are required.
A candidate detector may combine event-model scores, transient shape, spectral features, speech probability and ASR
alignment. These are proposed inputs, not a trained or evaluated classifier in this study. Keep a configurable policy for
natural breaths rather than treating every non-speech event as unwanted.
Build a human-labeled pilot with coughs, throat clears, breaths, clicks, quiet words and clean pauses, including examples
adjacent to speech. Tune for preserving intended speech. Select a threshold only after estimating event precision, recall
and false deletion rates on held-out recordings. A single reference edit cannot establish reliability.
Candidate events found in this source
Thirteen detectable acoustic events were at least 70% outside Premiere lexical timestamps. Eight fall in removed
material and five in retained material. This is deliberately weak candidate selection, not thirteen coughs. Recognition and
timing errors or quiet speech can explain some retained candidates.
Priority event 04 has an above-threshold core at source 257.70 to 257.99 s and peak 10 ms RMS -27.14 dBFS. Event 11
has a core at 485.59 to 485.72 s and peak -36.17 dBFS. Both were removed in the reference and are not silence by
energy. Neither is a validated cough or throat clear. Event 11 has weak energy extending toward 486.05 s, beyond its
core and into the kept side before fuller speech around 486.10 s. Never cut only the detected core and assume the
complete event is gone.
Use the thirteen review WAVs and candidate spectrogram atlas to label these sounds by listening. Event labels remain
provisional until then.
Review queue fields
For each candidate include source range, camera range, proposed output join, reason, raw transcript context, alignment
confidence, event scores, old and proposed padding, threshold sensitivity, competing boundaries, and a short
before-and-after audio snippet. Never replace an uncertain label with silence merely because ASR returned no words.

Implementation pseudocode
The following is a proposed contract, not executable production code. Intervals are half-open and source sample indices
are authoritative for audio. Every stage emits evidence and reversible decisions.
manifest = inspect_and_hash(camera, good_mic)
green = greenscreen_copy(camera, preserve_timestamps=True)
require_timing_match(green, camera)  # or explicit time map
anchors = match_speech_anchors(good_mic, camera.audio)
sync = fit_offset_and_drift(anchors)
if not sync_passes(sync): queue_sync_review(); stop_edit_apply()
time_map = compose_mic_camera_green_map(sync, green.map)
raw_asr = transcribe(good_mic)
aligned = align_with_uncertainty(raw_asr, good_mic)
events = detect_events_before_phrase_merge(good_mic, aligned)
retakes = propose_restarts(aligned, nearby_context=True)
for proposal in retakes:
    check_complete_take(proposal)
    check_unique_information_and_intentional_emphasis(proposal)
    proposal.boundaries = refine_both_sides(
        good_mic, aligned, events, candidate_pads=[(.10,.15)])
    route_uncertainty_to_review(proposal)
pauses = propose_contextual_pause_changes(aligned, retakes)
event_edits = propose_only_high_confidence_safe_events(events)
plan = combine_intervals(retakes, pauses, event_edits)
plan = resolve_overlap_and_protected_speech(plan)
assert_no_reintroduced_excluded_events(plan)
assert_no_unreviewed_uncertain_speech_deletion(plan)
edl, audit = export_plan(plan, time_map, retain_raw_times=True)
review = export_original_and_proposed_join_snippets(plan)
# Apply only approved plan to copies; originals remain unchanged.
rendered = render_copy(approved(plan), camera, good_mic, green)
validate_content_timing_joins_and_event_policy(rendered, audit)
Minimum plan record
Each decision needs an ID, source asset hash, microphone sample start/end, rational time base, mapped camera frame
or timestamp range, retained take ID, reason code, evidence references, confidence and review status. Store measured
boundary features separately from proposed settings. Include the exact algorithm version and parameter set so a later
run can reproduce the plan.
Suggested reason codes are RETAKE, ABANDONED_START, PAUSE_SHORTEN, COUGH_CANDIDATE,
THROAT_CLEAR_CANDIDATE and MANUAL_REVIEW. Only confirmed labels should drop the CANDIDATE suffix. A
rejection, keep decision or manual override should also remain in the audit log.

Quality assurance and acceptance
Structural and synchronization checks
- Verify all 15 reference clip mappings and all 14 reference deletions from the saved intervals before changing
 algorithms. Assert chronological, nonoverlapping ranges and equality between kept plus removed durations and
source duration, allowing only documented rounding.
- Check green-screen frame count and timestamps against the original. Test multiple mic/camera anchors and drift
 residuals. After rendering, compare known speech anchors across the entire output, not just its beginning.
- Report final sample count, audio duration, video duration and cumulative time-map error independently. Do not hide a
 mismatch by stretching or reinterpreting all timestamps.
Content and listening checks
- Listen to original context and proposed joins at every candidate cut. Check clipped consonants, plosives, repeated
 fragments, unnatural breath transitions, clicks and pace. The waveform and ASR work in this study cannot certify
these perceptual outcomes.
- Confirm that every removed repeated take is redundant and that the retained version is complete. Preserve
 meaningful hesitation and intentional repetition. Verify no unique fact, qualifier or instruction disappeared.
- Audit every event deletion separately. Review both detected events and a sample of retained material to catch false
 negatives. Label coughs and throat clears by listening, not transcript absence.
Evaluation design
Use this video for development and explanation, then evaluate on additional held-out raw recordings with different
delivery pace, background noise and enhancement settings. Split by recording, not neighboring snippets, to avoid
overfitting to one source. Report event precision and recall, false deletions of intended speech, missed retakes, join
ratings, reference interval disagreement and review workload separately.
A pilot acceptance gate should require zero confirmed intended-speech deletions in the reviewed pilot, all flagged cases
resolved, no unexplained sync drift, and satisfactory listening checks. Zero errors in a finite sample is not a reliability
guarantee. Select quantitative tolerance and confidence requirements with the human labels before production
deployment.
What is not established
All 14 internal cuts were measured and their raw boundary waveforms inspected, along with both head and tail waveform
plots, RMS and event evidence. No full perceptual listening pass was performed in this runtime. Cough and throat-clear
classifications remain unverified. RMS offsets are not phonetic labels: uncertainty includes the 10 ms grid, threshold
choice and output frame rounding. ASR boundaries can be uncertain by 100 ms or more. ASR can be wrong. Replay
disagreements are not definitive semantic errors. The proposed settings, event model and green-screen integration have
not been implemented or validated on held-out recordings. No claim of fully automatic editor-quality output follows from
this single example.
